stem: Use a calculator to find the {=W[i]} of ${=D[k]}^\circ 30'$. Round the result to four decimal places.
solution: Make sure the calculator is in degree mode.
Press the {=W[i]} key, enter {=D[k]}, press the degrees-minutes-seconds key (°'"), enter 30, press the key (°'") again, then press =.
Rounded to four decimal places, the {=W[i]} of ${=D[k]}^\circ 30'$ is {=T[k][i]}.
notes: Angles 15°30', 22°30', 67°30'; values computed by hand to 4 d.p. (tan 22.5 = sqrt2-1, tan 67.5 = sqrt2+1).
